comparisons.objective: Sets a proximity-sensor gap with a feeler leaf and secures it with a cam clamp; the candidate sets a gripper opening stop and locks a threaded adjuster.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2229 requires positioning a sensor against a third-body gauge and closing a lever; the candidate requires simultaneous coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque so a jam nut does not rotate the screw.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2229 checks a 1.00±0.25 mm gap, gauge removal/return, closed lever, and hands-off stability; the candidate checks a retained 90° opening after three released cycles, nut retention, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both set and retain an adjustment, but the candidate uniquely tests coupled screw–jam-nut counterholding and post-lock articulated cycling rather than gauge-mediated placement and cam clamping.

comparisons.objective: Assembles a door lever set and drives two mounting screws while keeping the outside lever level; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2018 combines hidden spindle/post insertion, opposing-part assembly, and stabilization of a large lever during separate screw driving; the candidate counterholds concentric threaded elements with two tools.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2018 requires seated roses, snug screws, and lever/hub level within 1° after release; the candidate requires a locked 90° stop retained through three actuation cycles.
comparisons.reason: The shared counterholding primitive is generic; separate-screw lockset assembly does not test preserving a threaded adjuster against its coaxial jam nut or verifying stop retention through cycles.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a DRG 80 gripper’s opening-stop screw to 90°, locks the setting, removes the tools, and verifies retained opening through repeated actuation. PR-216 instead captures an external reference angle with a bevel gauge, carries it to a board, and transfers it by drawing a guided line.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, coupled screw/jam-nut adjustment, and bimanual countertorque that prevents locknut tightening from disturbing the stop. PR-216 explicitly has no locking screw: it fits a passive-friction hinged blade to two faces, releases the blade gripper, transports the gauge without changing its angle, seats it, and guides a marker.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate rewards target opening accuracy, seated/retained nuts, hands-off repeat-cycle return, limited stop drift, tool withdrawal, and clearance, with loss revocation. PR-216 rewards fixture fit, visible release and retained angle during carry, board seating, then line coverage, tick proximity, straightness, gap/width limits, absence of stray marks, and nib clearance. All seven available spec versions provide numeric rubric details; none are materially missing for this comparison.
comparisons.reason: Both involve adjusting and retaining an angle, but PR-216 relies on passive hinge friction to transfer a measured angle into a drawn mark, whereas the candidate tests active preservation of a screw setting against jam-nut reaction followed by functional cycling; these are meaningfully different mechanisms, manipulation abilities, and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Torques a busbar lug bolt with a click wrench and stops at the click; the candidate establishes and locks an angular stop setting.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1501 tests socket seating and response to a one-shot torque signal without overpulling; the candidate tests simultaneous driver and thin-wrench countertorque on coupled threads.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1501 requires a seated click within 90–110% of target torque and penalizes unseated turning or overtorque; the candidate requires retained geometry and repeated gripper actuation rather than a torque endpoint.
comparisons.reason: Applying a specified tightening torque is materially different from preserving an adjustable screw position while tightening its jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Adjusts a cabinet hinge side cam for even reveals and closes the flap for inspection; the candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1865 uses a slotted driver on one of several cam heads and then articulates the door; the candidate coordinates two concentric tools against locknut reaction.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1865 checks closed reveal equality, flushness, no sag, and released stability; the candidate checks nut seating, 90° opening retention, drift, and three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both adjust and functionally inspect an articulated mechanism, but PR-1865 has no separate locking operation whose torque can disturb the chosen setting.

comparisons.objective: Installs a second rack into a parallel gripper at the correct tooth phase; the candidate adjusts an already assembled gripper's maximum opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1898 requires rack insertion, gear-tooth meshing, phase alignment, and coupled jaw motion; the candidate requires hex-driver and jam-nut wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1898 checks rack seating, jaw centering, and at least 15 mm symmetric opening; the candidate checks a locked 90° limit retained through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both concern grippers and functional motion, but gear-phase assembly and threaded stop calibration test different mechanisms and manipulation abilities.

comparisons.objective: Connects an M12 sensor cable while preventing a loose sensor barrel from rotating; the candidate adjusts a stop screw and locks it with its jam nut.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1540 directly holds a large sensor body while turning a coupling ring; the candidate must keep a driver seated in the screw while a second tool turns a concentric thin nut against it.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1540 succeeds when the connector is threaded tight, the cap is stored, and hands withdraw; the candidate additionally requires a retained angular setpoint and three released functional cycles.
comparisons.reason: The close shared feature is bimanual reaction-torque control, but connector assembly against a stabilized body does not test coupled screw–nut setpoint preservation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper’s angular stop, locks the concentric screw/jam-nut setting, then verifies repeated gripper motion. PR-2203 pulls a motor carriage against belt load, clamps it with two separate bolts, then measures belt deflection.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests simultaneous coaxial driver-and-wrench countertorque: jam-nut torque must not rotate the adjusted screw. PR-2203 tests holding a separate linear pull handle against belt restoring force while driving bolts; its complete Rig.step/Contacts.advance contains no bolt-torque-to-slide disturbance or coaxial reaction state.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening, seated/retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, ≤2° drift, tool withdrawal, and 1 s clearance. PR-2203 requires 1.40–1.95 mm deflection under 2.5 N, two ≥185 N clamps, ≤0.040 mm carriage drift, belt seating/alignment, parked driver, and clear arms; its task.json does not state the check duration, though implementation uses 0.45 s.
comparisons.reason: The shared adjust-lock-release pattern is generic, but the essential causal abilities differ: resisting locking torque transferred through concentric threaded elements versus resisting pre-existing belt tension until separate clamps develop friction. PR-2203’s source does not support the prior characterization that tightening reaction disturbs its adjustment; the distinction remains conditional on the candidate actually implementing the declared screw/nut torque coupling rather than a scripted lock state.

comparisons.objective: Squares a milling vise by sweeping an indicator, adjusting yaw, securing the swivel, and verifying it; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1799 requires dynamic indicator traversal, iterative alignment, and cam clamping; the candidate requires coaxial two-tool adjustment and counterholding during jam-nut tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1799 checks indicator span, sweep coverage, secured yaw, and released stability; the candidate checks opening angle, lock retention, drift, and repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: Both retain a setpoint after locking, but indicator-guided fixture alignment and cam securing are meaningfully different from countertorquing coupled threaded elements.

comparisons.objective: Adjusts a drum-brake star wheel through a slot until the drum has light drag; the candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2167 requires blind tooth engagement, levering, tool repositioning, and alternating adjustment with drum turning; the candidate requires concentric driver/wrench seating and opposing torque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2167 checks 22–28 clicks, light drag, no lockup, and tool release; the candidate checks a locked 90° opening retained across three cycles with limited drift.
comparisons.reason: Functional verification is shared, but detented blind clearance adjustment lacks the candidate's separate jam-nut locking and setpoint-preserving countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Pushes a hose fully onto a barb and tightens a worm-drive clamp; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1892 requires axial hose seating, clamp placement, socket engagement, and driver regrasping; the candidate requires simultaneous counterrotation of a screw and jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1892 checks hose depth, clamp location, snug/tight state, and released clearance; the candidate checks retained opening angle and repeated articulated operation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper stop screw, locks its concentric jam nut without shifting the setting, then cycles the gripper; PR-236 supports a gravity-loaded inspection arm at an angle and engages a separate indexed clamp knob.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous hex-driver and thin-wrench seating with countertorque against screw rotation caused by tightening its concentric nut; PR-236 instead supports an arm against gravity while turning a spatially separate knob whose reduced-order model supplies no lock reaction to the knob.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° setting retained within 3°, ≤2° drift over three released cycles, retained nuts, and 30 mm tool clearance; PR-236 requires the +15° arm aim, indexed lock engagement, and a two-second released hold within 3°/2° drift.
comparisons.reason: The essential tested causality differs: preserving a threaded adjustment against concentric locknut reaction is not subsumed by holding a payload against gravity while actuating a separate indexed lock, although both share generic set-lock-release primitives.

comparisons.objective: Feeds a cable through a gland, tightens its cap nut, and verifies pull retention; the candidate calibrates and locks an angular stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2145 combines deformable-cable insertion with threaded cap tightening and seal compression; the candidate uses two rigid tools to counterhold a screw during jam-nut locking.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2145 checks sheath depth, a bounded nut-turn window, 30 N pull retention, and crushing; the candidate checks angular accuracy, drift, nut retention, cycling, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both tighten threaded hardware and perform a retention test, but cable sealing/pull anchorage does not measure coupled setpoint preservation under locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Seals a carton seam and end tabs with a tape gun; the candidate adjusts and locks robot gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1893 requires tape-gun control, flap restraint, adhesive placement, tearing, and smoothing; the candidate requires precision two-tool threaded adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1893 checks seam coverage, alignment, torn tape, bonded tabs, flat flaps, and release; the candidate checks locked angular motion and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, mechanisms, manipulation skills, and observable outcomes are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Calibrates a torque-limiting clutch so it carries a light proof load and slips on a heavy one; the candidate sets a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1110 requires preload adjustment, selector operation, crank testing, and interpreting two load responses; the candidate requires jam-nut countertorque with coaxial tools.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1110 requires both proof tests at one unchanged preload and released stability; the candidate requires a retained 90° mechanical stop over three cycles.
comparisons.reason: PR-1110 tests load-dependent clutch calibration, not locking an angular adjuster while resisting tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Calibrates gripper force using a spring reference and zero/span/verify controls; the candidate mechanically adjusts a gripper's opening limit.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1645 requires controlled pad compression and ordered button operation while holding a reference load; the candidate requires two-tool threaded counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1645 checks zeroing, 8.5–10.5 mm spring compression, span capture, and unloaded verification; the candidate checks angular-stop locking and repeated motion retention.
comparisons.reason: Shared gripper context does not create overlap: force-sensor calibration and mechanical opening-stop locking test different abilities and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Moves two backlash-affected sliders to target readings and locks each dial; the candidate sets one gripper stop and secures it mechanically.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-779 requires reversal-aware compensation of display hysteresis and button presses; the candidate requires physical driver/wrench engagement and opposing torque on coupled threads.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-779 checks both displayed setpoints within ±2.5 mm and latched lock buttons; the candidate checks a locked 90° opening, ≤2° drift, and three actuation cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both contain setpoints and locking, but software-display backlash compensation with pushbutton latching does not test mechanical jam-nut countertorque or functional stop retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2209 seals a preloaded carton by peeling, paying out, applying, wrapping, and cutting tape from an ordinary loose roll.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests rigid two-tool screw-and-jam-nut countertorque plus articulated verification; PR-2209 tests flush tape-edge acquisition, flexible-material payout, pressure adhesion, end wrapping, and blade cutting.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained angular adjustment and repeated motion after tool withdrawal; PR-2209 grades connected tape coverage across 44 seam cells, two 35 mm end wraps, blade severing, detachment, and a two-second released seal.
comparisons.reason: Flexible tape sourcing, adhesion, wrapping, and cutting test a materially different ability from maintaining a threaded stop setting during locknut tightening; PR-2209 lacks a formal task.json, full demonstration, model run, media, and validated complete-task allowance, but those omissions do not create plausible overlap.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2208 turns over an upright taped carton, cuts three bottom-tape paths, opens four bottom flaps, and collapses the intact carton flat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial tool seating and coupled screw/nut countertorque; PR-2208 tests whole-carton turnover, guarded-blade path tracking, outward flap articulation, and intact wall-tube collapse.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° opening through three cycles with nuts retained and tools clear; PR-2208 requires measured turnover, all 158 cut cells, four flaps opened at least 150°, then all board vertices within a 24 mm slab for a one-second released hold.
comparisons.reason: Carton turnover, cutting, flap opening, and flattening do not exercise the candidate's coupled adjustment-preservation mechanism; PR-2208 lacks a formal task.json, complete-task run limit, full demo, model run, and media, but its tested outcome is still clearly unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and mechanically locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2207 operates a handheld dryer and manipulates articulated hair to dry exposed and occluded regions while the mannequin head remains fixed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests rigid driver/wrench counterholding and functional cycling; PR-2207 tests switch operation, dryer pickup and aiming, deformable lock separation, airflow exposure, and thermal control.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, nut retention, three repeatable cycles, limited drift, and released clearance; PR-2207 requires at least 90% water removal on every hair patch, temperature at most 50°C, fixed-head integrity, power off, parking, and a one-second released hold.
comparisons.reason: Deformable hair exposure and geometry-dependent drying are meaningfully different from threaded stop adjustment and jam-nut locking; PR-2207 lacks a formal task.json, demonstrated full-task allowance, full demo, model run, and media, without making the novelty distinction ambiguous.

comparisons.objective: PR-1784 safely isolates and depressurizes a pneumatic manifold, removes a tube from a push-to-connect fitting, inserts a blanking plug, and verifies retention; the candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop and verifies retained motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1784 requires lockout, dump verification, collet depression while extracting a flexible tube, plug insertion, and a pull test; the candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench seating, bimanual countertorque that preserves a screw setting, tool withdrawal, and articulated cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1784 grades safe release history, tube removal, plug seating/grip, a 15 N retention test, and clearance; the candidate grades 90° adjustment accuracy, jam-nut locking, three repeatable cycles, limited drift, hardware retention, and released clearance.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities and outcomes are meaningfully different despite both involving industrial hardware and hands-off retention; no material PR-1784 rubric detail is missing, while the candidate discloses that nut 74's precise role is unspecified.

comparisons.objective: Draft task unlatches an Ethernet plug in a crowded panel and transfers it to another port; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2210 requires small spring-tab depression, constrained plug withdrawal/insertion, flexible-cable management, and avoiding neighboring plugs; the candidate requires two-tool threaded counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2210 proposes source release before withdrawal, target seating and latch re-engagement, neighbor retention, and a released hold; the candidate checks angular-stop retention and cycling.
comparisons.reason: Connector unlatching and insertion in cable clutter are mechanically and observably different from screw–jam-nut calibration.

comparisons.objective: PR-1405 hand-tightens a spin-on oil filter from pre-contact to the specified post-contact angular range without under- or overtightening; the candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper stop before functional cycling.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1405 tests controlled whole-can wrist rotation, regrasping, gasket-contact referencing, and release; the candidate tests simultaneous hex-driver counterholding and thin-jam-nut wrenching against coupled reaction torque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1405 grades final rotation past gasket contact, peak overtightening, hand-driven motion, thread retention, and release; the candidate grades target opening, locked retention, repeat-cycle return, drift, nut retention, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both regulate a rotational setting, but PR-1405 does not test preserving an adjustment screw while locking a coupled jam nut or verifying an articulated mechanism afterward; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: PR-1570 closes an adjustable wrench snugly on a nylon nut, loosens the nut in the safe direction, and sets the wrench down; the candidate sets and locks an opening-stop screw on a gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1570 tests thumbwheel adjustment, jaw-clearance control, correct fixed-jaw loading, breakaway pulling, and tool removal; the candidate tests coaxial driver seating plus simultaneous wrench seating and countertorque to prevent setting drift.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1570 grades loosened angle, loose-jaw and wrong-direction faults, wrench set-down, and release; the candidate grades angular accuracy, jam-nut seating, repeated retained motion, stop drift, hardware retention, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: The shared wrench-and-nut primitive is insufficient for overlap because PR-1570 tests adjustable-wrench fit and pull direction, whereas the candidate tests coupled two-tool lockup without disturbing a setting; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Dials a three-number padlock combination and pulls the shackle open; the candidate adjusts and locks industrial gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2158 requires precise multi-turn dial control with reversals and regrasping on a swinging body; the candidate requires coupled two-tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2158 checks successive wheel-gate alignment, shackle release, remaining on the hasp, and released stillness; the candidate checks locked opening angle and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Rotary precision is the only generic commonality; the mechanisms, required coordination, and success outcomes differ materially.

comparisons.objective: PR-771 closes an edge joint between two boards by pumping a one-hand bar clamp and leaves sustained clamping force; the candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop and verifies its motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-771 tests placing a clamp around boards, repeated trigger strokes, board alignment, and force buildup; the candidate tests precision screw adjustment, thin-nut wrenching, bimanual counterholding, tool withdrawal, and lever-driven cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-771 grades jaw and joint gaps, at least 20 N clamping force, board alignment, release, stillness, and loss from the table; the candidate grades a 90° setting, lock retention, three repeatable cycles, drift, retained nuts, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: The tasks share only generic force application and hands-off verification, not the same mechanism, manipulation, or outcome; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Selects and installs the matching driver bit, power-tightens a drawer knob, and returns the tool; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1288 requires bit-shape selection, bit insertion, powered screw engagement, workpiece stabilization, and tool parking; the candidate requires manual two-tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1288 checks mounted-bit identity, powered axial screw feed, knob closure, a 5 N hold test, motor-off release, and tool return; the candidate checks retained angular opening and cycling.
comparisons.reason: Powered fastening after bit selection is a different tested ability from adjusting a screw setpoint and preventing its rotation during jam-nut locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop and verifies retained articulation; pr-1690 mounts a bicycle tire bead into a rim while avoiding tube damage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench counterholding so jam-nut torque does not disturb a screw setting, followed by tool withdrawal and lever-actuated cycling. pr-1690 requires bimanual bead depression into the drop center and controlled rolling of a deformable tire section over the flange.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained 90° opening, seated/retained nuts, repeated return accuracy, limited drift, and hands-off clearance. pr-1690 grades bead seating, valve alignment, hand clearance, partial bead-channel progress, and leak/pinch avoidance; its versions provide numeric thresholds.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, manipulated mechanisms, force-control problem, and observable outcomes test meaningfully different abilities; shared bimanual coordination is only a generic primitive.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an angular-gripper stop while preserving its setting, then verifies retained motion; pr-890 drives a started bracket bolt to seated contact with a ratchet in confined access.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver countertorque and thin-jam-nut wrenching on a coupled screw/nut setting, followed by functional cycling. pr-890 requires ratchet pickup, socket alignment, and repeated short drive/return strokes that advance one threaded fastener between walls.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades target opening accuracy, nut retention, post-lock cycle repeatability, stop drift, tool withdrawal, and clearance. The latest pr-890 spec grades axial bolt advance, actual head/bracket seating, thread integrity, and a 0.5-second seated dwell; torque and cycle counts are diagnostic, although earlier versions required six productive cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both involve tools and threaded hardware, but pr-890 tests confined ratcheting to seat a fastener, whereas the candidate tests preservation of an adjustable setpoint against locknut reaction and hands-off functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts robot-gripper hardware; this record closes a used needle's hinged safety sheath and deposits the syringe in a sharps tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual coaxial tool engagement and countertorque; the record requires one-handed surface-assisted sheath latching while avoiding the exposed needle.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained opening and lock integrity; the record checks a positively latched sheath, safe clearances, tray placement, release, and no forbidden needle contact.
comparisons.reason: The record tests sharps-safe one-handed latching and disposal, with no adjustable setting or coupled screw/nut mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; this record inserts and secures a drill bit in a keyed chuck.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds an adjustment screw with a driver while turning a thin jam nut; the record stabilizes a drill and keeps a chuck key meshed against increasing separating force.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° stop across repeated actuation; the record requires a centered, captured bit that resists torque and pull, with the key removed.
comparisons.reason: The shared need to maintain tool engagement under torque is generic; chuck clamping does not test preserving a calibrated setting against jam-nut reaction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an end-effector stop; this record removes, wipes, reinserts, rereads, and reports an engine-oil dipstick level.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coupled rotary tools and countertorque; the record performs long thin-part extraction/insertion, wiping, visual level reading, and report-token placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks mechanical retention through cycles; the record checks a valid clean reread, correct level report, reseated dipstick, and released rag/objects.
comparisons.reason: Oil measurement and reporting exercise contamination-aware extraction and perception, not mechanical adjustment or locking.

comparisons.objective: Both establish a machine setting and secure it, but the candidate sets an angular opening stop while this record positions a cylinder slot sensor at its switching-band midpoint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous concentric driver and wrench action with countertorque against jam-nut reaction; the record drags and clamps one sensor through a single seated hex driver using LED feedback.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° stop retained over three close-open cycles; the record requires sensor position within tolerance, clamp resistance, and correct LED switching when the cylinder moves.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record, but it does not test the candidate's defining coupled screw/jam-nut counterholding ability; its setting is translational and feedback-located through one tool.

comparisons.objective: Remove an air-fryer basket from its drawer and place it on a heat-proof mat; versions use either a slide-under-hooks release or a held release button.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed basket release, handle lifting, transport and placement while avoiding hot surfaces; the later version coordinates holding a button while lifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Basket released, placed flat and still on the mat, button returned where applicable, robot clear, with hot contact, bypass lifting or dropping causing zero. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque that preserves a gripper stop setting through jam-nut locking and repeated actuation, not keyed release and safe transport of a hot basket.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper motion limit; this record releases a camera plate from a cam-clamped mount and transfers it to a pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two coaxial tools to resist lock reaction; the record rotates a release cam, clears a separate rear lip, and supports a payload during removal.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate verifies retained opening after cycles; the record checks cam release, mount clearance, supported upright pad placement, release, and stability without dropping.
comparisons.reason: Cam release and retained-payload dismounting test disengagement and transfer rather than calibration, countertorque, or post-lock functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Brake a coasting flywheel before entering its guard zone, keep it restrained while unscrewing its clamp nut, and place the nut in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate a sprung friction-brake lever, verify zero speed, sustain restraint against wheel rotation, unscrew a threaded nut and transfer it safely.
comparisons.success_condition: Wheel below 0.15 rad/s before approach, nut unscrewed by at least two turns and removed, then released upright in the tray while the wheel remains stopped and the brake returns up; premature guard-zone entry zeros the trial. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Both tasks involve counterholding and a nut, but this record tests stored-energy braking and threaded fastener removal from a rotating assembly, whereas the candidate tests preserving an adjustable stop while tightening a jam nut and verifying retained motion.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper stop; this record clamps wood in a screw vise and saws a 150 mm piece.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs fine coupled screw/nut countertorque; the record tightens a vise and maintains an unguided saw cut through material.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained angular function; the record checks prior clamping, physical separation, a 150±1 mm retained length, intact positioning, and saw clearance.
comparisons.reason: Workholding and material removal to length test forceful cutting accuracy, not an adjustable mechanism's lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Place two setting blocks at marked quarter points and install a glass unit in a window frame so it stands on both blocks without touching the sill.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precise block placement followed by constrained glass insertion, including tilted room-side insertion in later versions, alignment against a stop, controlled support and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Glass stands released and still in the rebate on both correctly placed blocks, centred and upright, with any sill contact, severe tilt or loss causing zero. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: This tests support preparation and collision-free insertion of a fragile panel into a narrow frame, not coupled screw adjustment, locknut countertorque or post-lock actuation retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper’s adjustable opening stop to 90°, secures it with a jam nut, and verifies retained jaw motion over repeated cycles. PR-2248 instead positions a gauge block, closes a micrometer to measurement contact using its ratchet, and locks the reading.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests simultaneous driver counterholding and wrench tightening so locknut reaction does not disturb a screw setting, followed by tool withdrawal and articulated cycling. PR-2248 tests precise block placement, ratchet-only contact with counted slip clicks, avoidance of thimble overtravel, and lock-lever actuation; it does not require concentric two-tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires opening-angle accuracy, seated/retained nuts, three repeat cycles with limited stop drift, and hands-off clearance. PR-2248 requires the block remain aligned between the faces, a 20.000 mm gap tolerance, at least three valid ratchet clicks, lever locking, no squeeze or fall, and hands-off stability. Missing details: candidate hardware dimensions and torque/friction parameters remain future declared assumptions, while PR-2248 explicitly does not model the ratchet torque limit; neither omission obscures the different tested outcomes.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve setting and locking an adjustable mechanism, the candidate’s defining ability is preserving a screw-set gripper stop against jam-nut reaction and proving cyclic retention, whereas PR-2248’s defining ability is controlled micrometer contact through ratchet slip and measurement locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts gripper travel; this record removes a cordless-drill battery and places it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds a screw during jam-nut tightening; the record simultaneously squeezes two release buttons while stabilizing the drill and sliding the pack along rails.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks angle retention after locking; the record checks remembered dual-button release, pack separation, tray placement, drill displacement, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Simultaneous latch release and sliding extraction test a different bimanual mechanism and endpoint.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both faces of a kitchen knife on a whetstone and return it safely to the chopping block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain a 13–22° bevel angle and near-level blade while making edge-leading heel-to-tip abrasive strokes, reorienting for both faces and safely releasing the knife.
comparisons.success_condition: Later versions require ten qualifying strokes and coverage of at least 12 of 16 edge points per face in simulation, or measured sharpness at three of four points in reality, plus a stable edge-away put-down for full score. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both tasks regulate an angle, knife sharpening tests sustained abrasive contact, stroke direction and full-edge coverage rather than setting and mechanically locking an articulated stop against tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts robot hardware; this record rinses highlighted teeth, evacuates water, and returns dental tools.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses concentric rotary tools; the record coordinates irrigator coverage and suction placement, including timed post-rinse clearance and tool return.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained mechanical motion; the record checks crown wetting, water recovery, spill limits, near-dry final state, tool poses, release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Coordinated liquid delivery and evacuation have different manipulation, hazards, and observable outcomes from threaded adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Place a nickel interconnect strip on a 2×2 battery pack, spot-weld it to all four cells, and return the welder to its holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Handle and align a thin strip, regrasp and orient a two-probe welder, make four precise dwell contacts, and restore tools without disturbing the pack.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit covers centred strip placement, four 0.2-second dual-probe weld contacts, and reseating the welder; full score additionally requires both arms clear/home and all parts still for one second, while pack knockover or lost parts score zero. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: This tests thin-part placement and repeated localized joining with a handheld welder, not counterholding a screw during jam-nut locking or verifying a retained gripper opening through repeated cycles.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; this record bleeds air from a brake caliper through repeated pedal-and-bleeder cycles.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate applies simultaneous countertorque at one coaxial assembly; the record coordinates a pedal with a wrench at a separate valve, enforcing close-before-release timing.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained opening angle after three cycles; the record scores air removed and permanently fails if pedal return draws air through an open bleeder.
comparisons.reason: Both use repeated actuation and a wrench, but brake bleeding tests hydraulic sequencing and state reduction rather than preservation of a mechanical setting.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures a gripper stop; this record mounts a shaft between fixed and spring-loaded bench centres.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coaxial driver/wrench countertorque; the record holds a tailstock lever retracted while seating and pivoting a shaft onto two conical points.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks locked angular travel; the record checks both centre points properly seated, lever returned, shaft still, hands clear, and no damaging ram/drop.
comparisons.reason: Lever-held precision shaft seating tests alignment and compliant insertion, not threaded setting and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Both concern robot end effectors, but the candidate adjusts a gripper's opening stop while this record mounts a separate suction tool on a quick-change flange.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds an adjustment screw while tightening a jam nut; the record aligns a tool plate to flange features while another hand turns or presses a locking-ring lever.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained target angle over repeated articulation; the record requires the selected tool seated and locked on the flange, hanging unsupported with hands withdrawn.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual holding-while-locking is generic; flange registration and payload latching do not test preserving a screw-defined motion limit against locknut reaction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures gripper hardware; this record proves a voltage detector before and after testing a conductor and tags or withdraws appropriately on failure.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two rotary hand tools; the record balances a long stick-mounted detector, presses tester controls, contacts target points, and reacts to indicator state.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained mechanical adjustment; the record checks valid pre/post proofs, correct test behavior, safe final separation, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Electrical-test procedural verification and long-tool handling do not overlap the candidate's coupled adjustment mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks an opening limit; this record fills and assembles a moka pot for brewing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a driver and wrench with countertorque; the record pours to a fill level, inserts the basket, and rotates a large threaded chamber to its seat.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks stop drift across cycles; the record checks water below the valve, basket presence, snug top, limited spill, safe carafe placement, and release.
comparisons.reason: The shared threaded rotation is only a generic primitive; moka-pot assembly has no calibrated setting, jam nut, counterholding, or functional retention test.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts gripper travel; this record removes a drawer from telescoping slides.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses precision coaxial tools; the record operates two opposite-sense release levers while pulling and supporting the drawer off its rails.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks a locked 90° stop through cycles; the record checks both slide releases, complete drawer removal or placement, hand clearance, and stability.
comparisons.reason: Opposed latch actuation during extraction tests coordinated release and support, not mechanical calibration or locking.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures robot hardware; this record removes individual gnocchi from simmering water after they float and turns off the burner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs coupled rotary adjustment; the record tracks asynchronous food-state changes and uses a slotted spoon for timed retrieval without direct contact.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained angular motion; the record checks timely removal to a plate, burner shutdown, release/stability, and no gripper-food contact.
comparisons.reason: State-triggered utensil retrieval and heat shutdown are unrelated to threaded adjustment and countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper stop to a specified angle; this record fits opposed tapered shims behind a door jamb until snug without bowing it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate resists jam-nut torque with a coaxial driver; the record incrementally drives two opposed wedges, senses fit, and balances contact pressure from both wall faces.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks lock retention over actuation cycles; the record checks shim overlap, near-zero free gap, bounded jamb bow, rest, and hand clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both preserve a target while securing it, but opposed-wedge fit and jamb straightness test force-balanced insertion rather than coupled threaded countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts a robot gripper; this record tests two machine light curtains across their full fields and tags the failed unit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses concentric rotary tools; the record carries test rods level and tip-first through multiple lanes while observing machine responses and placing a tag.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate checks retained stop angle and locking; the record checks complete field sweeps, correct failure identification/tagging, rods removed, hand clearance, and a stable dwell.
comparisons.reason: Safety-field coverage testing and conditional tagging have different physical actions and outcomes from gripper-stop adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a fixed tool tip by touching one reference point from four sufficiently different wrist orientations; candidate instead sets and locks a gripper opening stop, then cycles it to verify retention.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-827 tests precise single-tool pivoting about a stationary contact with stable one-second holds. The candidate tests coaxial driver/wrench seating, bimanual countertorque, setting preservation during jam-nut locking, tool withdrawal, and lever actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-827 awards 0.25 per qualified contact pose, requiring four distinct axes for full score. The candidate grades released opening accuracy, installed nut retention, three repeat cycles, limited drift, and one-second tool/gripper clearance, with prerequisite revocation and loss failures.
comparisons.reason: The tasks test meaningfully different abilities: multi-orientation TCP contact calibration versus mechanically locking an adjustable stop against tightening reaction and proving hands-off retained motion.

comparisons.objective: Select and mount the undamaged grinding wheel with the complete ordered flange/blotter stack, tighten it safely, and verify secure mounting; candidate instead adjusts and locks an already-assembled gripper opening stop at a target angle.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-871 emphasizes inspection choice, repeated coaxial insertion of keyed and annular parts, spindle restraint, and torque-window tightening. The candidate emphasizes simultaneous driver-and-wrench counterholding so a screw setting does not rotate while its jam nut is locked, followed by tool withdrawal and articulation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-871 scores ordered stack completion, nut seating below an irreversible overtorque limit, released spindle-lock/hand clearance, low slip in a braked spin, and limited axial motion under tug. The candidate scores target-angle accuracy, nut retention, three close-open returns, at most 2° drift, and sustained 30 mm clearance, with revocation on locking or retention failure.
comparisons.reason: Both include nut tightening, clearance, and post-tightening functional checks, but PR-871 tests safe ordered wheel-stack assembly and clamp adequacy, whereas the candidate's defining ability is preserving an adjustable screw setting against coupled locknut reaction.

comparisons.objective: Angle a full-size click-lock vinyl tile tongue into an installed row and lower it flat to lock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-edge insertion into a narrow groove while coordinating the unsupported near edge, followed by contact-driven lowering and locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Tile ends flat, aligned to the row and spacer, with its long click joint fully engaged and no raised/open seam; incomplete engagement earns only partial credit.
comparisons.reason: Its tested ability is long compliant-profile edge engagement and lowering, not torque-preserving screw adjustment, jam-nut locking, or retained cycle verification.

comparisons.objective: Close a tool-chest lid while holding its ratchet-stay release and avoiding a slam or pinch zone.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sustained release actuation plus controlled lowering of a gravity-loaded hinged lid.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid reaches the rim slowly, the knob returns home, hands clear the chest, and the state remains still for one second; excessive edge speed or pinch-zone entry forces zero.
comparisons.reason: Although both use articulated motion and bimanual coordination, this record tests guarded lid lowering under a held release rather than preserving and locking an adjustable stop against tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot gripper’s opening stop at 90° and verifies retained actuation; PR-757 strips 8–12 mm of insulation from a cable using a lever-operated benchtop station.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, coupled screw–jam-nut countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and articulated cycling. PR-757 requires depth-controlled cable insertion, sustained lever depression against spring/cutting force, and straight cable extraction while the blades remain closed.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores angular accuracy, nut retention, limited stop drift across three cycles, and one-second hands-off clearance, with loss revocation. PR-757 scores insertion progress, completed stripping length, lever release, and gripper clearance, with explicit cut/pull force checks in its latest version.
comparisons.reason: The tasks share bimanual force coordination and release verification only at a generic level; one tests preserving a precision mechanical adjustment during locknut tightening and subsequent cyclic retention, while the other tests cable positioning and material removal under a held cutting mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Safely rout a curved board edge by bracing on a starting pin, pivoting onto the bearing, and feeding against cutter rotation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Two-hand free-board control against cutter forces, pivoted engagement, curved feeding, and hazard clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified curved length is routed in the safe direction after a pin-braced start, the board clears the cutter, and hands remain outside the 3-inch hazard zone; an off-pin first bite irreversibly scores zero.
comparisons.reason: This is force-controlled workpiece feeding around a guarded cutting tool, with no adjustable screw setting, jam-nut countertorque, or post-lock motion-retention test.

comparisons.objective: Install an O-ring over a hydraulic plug thread into its groove without excessive stretch or twist.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled elastomer stretching, axial transfer over threads, square release, and seating correction.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring is fully seated and released in the groove, remains within the 50% stretch and 90° roll limits, and has no side left on the thread; damage limits force zero.
comparisons.reason: The record tests deformable seal handling and damage avoidance, whereas the candidate tests coupled rigid screw/nut adjustment and retained articulated function.

comparisons.objective: Roll puff pastry into an even 3 mm sheet using a spacer-ring rolling pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual level rolling over repeated passes to control deformable-sheet thickness and length.
comparisons.success_condition: Sheet is at least 20 cm long, at least 90% lies within 2.5–3.5 mm, lateral thickness averages are even within 0.5 mm, and the pin is released level.
comparisons.reason: It measures distributed deformable-material shaping, not coaxial tool seating, countertorque locking, or retained mechanical-stop adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Tighten fifteen pool balls into a legal rack, place the head ball on the foot spot, and lift the triangle away without disturbing them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compacting free-rolling objects inside a frame and extracting that frame vertically without imparting lateral motion.
comparisons.success_condition: All 30 neighboring pairs are within 0.5 mm, the head ball is within 5 mm of the spot, the rack and hands are clear, and balls are still; disturbance during rack removal is latched.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is group compaction and disturbance-free frame removal, unrelated to preserving a threaded angular setting through jam-nut tightening and repeated actuation.

comparisons.objective: Start a handheld 3D scanner and cover a cast housing’s outer surface and top while maintaining tracking.
comparisons.physical_skill: Button actuation, sustained scanner pose/standoff/orientation control, viewpoint planning, and coordinated turntable motion.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 95% surface coverage including the top, with scanner and fingertips 3 cm clear for one second; part displacement, scanner contact, or a drop forces zero.
comparisons.reason: This record evaluates active sensing and coverage planning rather than mechanical adjustment, counterholding, locking, and functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Raise an unpowered robot link to its zero mark and insert a calibration pin so it remains at zero after release.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual gravity-load support, visual/physical hole alignment, and transverse pin insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin is home, link remains within 1° of zero and still for one second, and both grippers are at least 30 mm clear; excessive link speed forces zero.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot setup and retained alignment, but this record aligns holes and inserts a load-bearing pin; it does not set a continuous stop with a screw, counterhold a jam nut, or verify repeated motion return.

comparisons.objective: Take a tympanic temperature by seating a covered probe, pressing Measure, holding it steady through the reading, and laying it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine probe-to-canal alignment, steady unsupported holding during button actuation, and controlled withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid three-second reading is completed without unseating or exceeding 1.5 mm/3° motion, then the thermometer is released still on the table; excessive insertion or dropping forces zero.
comparisons.reason: It tests steady medical probe placement through a timed measurement, not threaded stop adjustment, countertorque locking, or cyclic retention.

comparisons.objective: Plant and backfill a delicate pepper seedling so its root plug is level, upright, evenly surrounded, firm, and undamaged; the candidate instead sets and locks a robot-gripper opening stop and verifies retained motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: Seedling planting requires holding a fragile root plug while distributing and firming granular material without damaging the stem or leaves. The candidate requires coaxial driver and wrench seating, coupled screw–jam-nut countertorque, tool withdrawal, and articulated test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2106 grades plug tilt/depth, four-sided soil level, hole fill, firmness under a side push, spill, release, and plant damage. The candidate grades 90° opening accuracy, nut retention, three repeat cycles, stop drift, tool/hand clearance, and hardware or fixture loss. All available versions provide numeric thresholds; no material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The shared need for bimanual stabilization is generic; granular backfilling around a fragile plant tests materially different manipulation and outcomes from preserving a mechanical adjustment while locking a jam nut and verifying cyclic retention.

comparisons.objective: Disinfect an IV connector hub for 15 seconds, then seat a syringe and complete a measured saline flush; the candidate instead sets and locks a robot gripper opening stop and verifies retained articulation.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1013 tests sustained frictional wiping, contamination-aware sequencing, coaxial syringe seating, and plunger actuation. It does not test concentric screw/jam-nut counterholding, preservation of an angular adjustment under locking torque, or post-lock mechanism cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1013 requires 300 valid scrub samples, no premature syringe contact, aligned seating, and ultimately at least 5 mL discharged with at least 4.5 mL collected; partial scores distinguish cleaning, seating, and flushing. The candidate requires a released 90° opening within tolerance, seated/retained nuts, three repeat cycles with limited drift, tool withdrawal, and one-second clearance. No material rubric details are missing from the available versions.
comparisons.reason: The tasks share fine alignment and tool handling only at a generic level; infection-control wiping and fluid-line access do not exercise the candidate's defining ability to preserve a mechanical stop while locking it against reaction torque and validate retained motion.

comparisons.objective: Install a circlip in a loose shaft’s groove, rotate it to verify seating, and put down the pliers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled ring spreading with dedicated pliers, shaft stabilization, groove seating, and relative rotation against friction.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring remains undamaged, seated and closed in the groove, rotates at least 15° relative to the restrained shaft, and pliers are removed and released; overspread or bending forces zero.
comparisons.reason: This shares counterholding and a post-installation functional check, but tests elastic retaining-ring installation and relative rotation, not screw-set regulation preserved through concentric jam-nut torque and repeated gripper cycles.

comparisons.objective: Orient and insert an emergency-stop button through a keyed panel hole, then secure it with a rear locking ring.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed rotational alignment, through-panel insertion, bimanual front-side stabilization, and rear ring threading.
comparisons.success_condition: Button is seated with its tab aligned, locking ring turns 165–185° and lies within 0.5 mm of the panel, and both parts remain still with grippers clear for one second.
comparisons.reason: It includes bimanual threaded locking, but the setting is a binary keyed panel insertion; it does not regulate a continuous stop angle, counterhold a coupled adjustment screw against locknut reaction, or verify retained actuation.

comparisons.objective: Replace two thin shelf-edge price tickets while preserving the third ticket and nearby cans.
comparisons.physical_skill: Opening a sprung clear strip, extracting nearly flush thin cards, inserting replacements into a narrow channel, and releasing them securely.
comparisons.success_condition: Both old tickets are in the waste tray, matching new tickets are seated under the correct cans, the untouched ticket remains seated, hands withdraw, and the assembly remains still; tipping a can forces zero.
comparisons.reason: This is thin-card extraction and insertion under a sprung cover, with no threaded adjustment, torque preservation, or articulated retention test.

comparisons.objective: Place a phone, watch, and earbuds case on their matching positions of a three-device charger and leave all charging.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object contact/alignment, magnetic placement, flexible watch-band handling, and indicator visibility management.
comparisons.success_condition: Each released device charges uninterrupted for five seconds with a visible indicator while the stand remains within 5 mm and 5° of its starting pose.
comparisons.reason: It tests repeated device placement and charging confirmation rather than coupled screw/nut manipulation or retaining an adjusted mechanical stop.

comparisons.objective: Push an evacuated blood tube onto a holder already connected to a training-arm vein, fill it, remove it, and place it in a tray without moving the needle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization of a needle holder against insertion/extraction forces and precise tube exchange.
comparisons.success_condition: Stopper is pierced, tube fills to at least 90%, is removed and released in the tray, while the holder remains held and needle motion stays within 2 mm; loss of stabilization forces zero.
comparisons.reason: Although it tests counterholding against axial reaction, its outcome is a filled and removed tube with needle stability, not angular setting preservation through jam-nut tightening and repeated actuation.

comparisons.objective: Break open an inert scored ampoule using a protective opener while retaining the cap and keeping the body upright.
comparisons.physical_skill: Protective-tool alignment, controlled breakaway torque, fragment/cap capture, and safe release.
comparisons.success_condition: Native neck joint breaks, cap remains fully captured, body returns upright to its holder, opener returns to its rack, and both remain released and still; neck/cap contact, excessive tilt, escape, or drop forces zero.
comparisons.reason: This tests controlled fracture and captive retention; prototype break-force calibration is explicitly missing, but the objective and tested ability remain clearly different from threaded stop adjustment and lock verification.

comparisons.objective: Clamp an aluminium workpiece, drill a marked through-hole on a bench drill press, and leave the machine safe; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop, then verifies that setting through repeated actuation.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-776 includes holding a loose plate against clamp-pad rotation, tightening a hold-down screw, operating motor controls and a capstan, and maintaining clearance from a rotating chuck. The candidate instead requires coaxial driver engagement plus wrench engagement on a coupled screw and thin jam nut, bimanual countertorque that preserves a calibrated setting, tool withdrawal, and articulated functional testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-776 awards full credit for a clamped plate, a 5 mm through-hole within 5 mm of the punch mark, no hand/wrist entry within 5 cm of the rotating bit or chuck, and a stopped drill with quill raised; partial and spoil outcomes are defined. The candidate grades retained 90° adjustment, nut retention, three repeat cycles, at most 2° drift, and hands/tools clear for one second. No material rubric details are missing from the available versions.
comparisons.reason: Both involve resisting rotation while tightening, but PR-776 uses clamping only as workholding prerequisite for drilling; it does not test coupled adjuster/jam-nut locking where tightening must preserve a setpoint and subsequent mechanism cycles must retain it.

comparisons.objective: Hold a shelf against an irregular wall and trace its profile with a pencil compass; the candidate instead adjusts and locks a gripper stop before testing its retained opening.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1871 requires sustained surface-guided compass motion, simultaneous shelf stabilization, tool orientation, and continuous precision marking. The candidate requires concentric two-tool engagement, coordinated countertorque that prevents screw drift, wrench regrasping, and subsequent lever actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1871 grades a continuous edge-to-edge curved line at 14 stations, profile bend, compass placement, shelf/tool stillness, clearance, and loss events. The candidate grades opening-angle tolerance, locknut seating and retention, repeated-cycle return, drift, and released clearance. All available versions specify the relevant numeric rubric; no material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both use two hands and require stabilizing one element while manipulating a tool, tracing a surface profile into a continuous accurate mark is a different tested ability from counterholding a coupled adjustment during locknut tightening and proving retained mechanical function.

comparisons.objective: Attach a detachable handle to a saucepan, prove it load-bearing, carry the pan to a trivet, and release it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rim/jaw mechanism engagement, latch closure, load-path verification, and stable transport through the attached handle.
comparisons.success_condition: Pan is lifted solely through the locked handle for one second, then placed within 20 mm of the trivet center and released stable for two seconds; direct support, slip, or excessive penetration invalidates credit.
comparisons.reason: Its functional verification is load-bearing transport after latch assembly, not preserving an adjustable stop while tightening a jam nut or checking return angle over repeated cycles.

comparisons.objective: Refit a rack-server air shroud by inserting both front tabs under the fan cage and lowering the rear to seat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual handling of a large rigid duct, simultaneous dual-tab insertion, constrained lowering, and release among obstacles.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tabs extend at least 3 mm into their slots, all four shroud corners lie within 2 mm of the chassis floor, grippers clear by 3 cm, and the shroud remains still for one second.
comparisons.reason: This tests large-part dual-tab insertion and seating in a server chassis, with no threaded tool use, countertorque regulation, or retained angular-stop calibration.

comparisons.objective: Remove a cracked robot cover from keyhole posts, discard it, and install and slide-lock a replacement cover.
comparisons.physical_skill: Unlocking and locking a three-post keyhole interface, cover handling, swap sequencing, and precise planar sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Old cover is off and in the tray, new cover is aligned and locked at the slot ends, grippers clear, and both covers stay still for one second; a cover falling off the table forces zero.
comparisons.reason: It tests binary keyhole slide-lock cover replacement, not continuous screw adjustment preserved against locknut torque and validated by repeated articulation.

comparisons.objective: Remove a toy brick jammed on the robot’s own gripper and demonstrate restored closing and opening.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual self-maintenance, obstruction extraction from a snug fit, and post-repair actuator testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Initial blocked closure is established, brick clears the affected fingers, the gripper subsequently closes below 2 mm and opens above 85 mm, with sustained clearance; a lost or damaged brick scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Both require post-maintenance motion verification, but this record tests obstruction removal and restoration of finger travel, not setting and locking a precise opening stop with coupled screw/nut countertorque.

comparisons.objective: Fit color-matched caps to four pens and sort the completed pens into marked areas; the candidate sets, locks, and functionally verifies an industrial gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-360 tests color matching, repeated coaxial cap insertion, bimanual part handling, release, and sorting. It lacks screw adjustment, wrench/driver countertorque, setpoint preservation during locknut tightening, and articulated retention testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-360 gives per-pen credit for a matching cap retained after insertion and hands-clear dwell, plus placement credit when the released capped pen rests inside its color area; full score requires all four capped and sorted. The candidate instead requires specified opening accuracy, installed nuts, three repeat cycles, bounded drift, and released clearance. Available versions disclose that simulated cap retention uses a pose-preserving joint and that physical force qualification is unverified; otherwise the scoring rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: Generic insertion, bimanual handling, and release are insufficient for overlap: PR-360 measures repeated closure assembly and color sorting, not torque-coupled adjustment locking or preservation of a mechanical setting through functional cycles.

comparisons.objective: Reattach a detached live wrist camera through a tapered sliding shoe and spring-loaded retaining tooth, then release it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Self-referential bimanual alignment, guided insertion into a wrist channel, passive-latch engagement, and retention verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Camera reaches within 5 mm and 5° of its optical target, passes through the guide, seats with the tooth engaged, and remains aligned with the assisting TCP over 80 mm away for two seconds.
comparisons.reason: It tests guided sensor-module insertion and passive latch retention, not an adjustable stop, jam-nut counterholding, or repeated return-angle stability.

comparisons.objective: Clamp locking pliers onto a tube past their lock point and leave them hanging securely without support.
comparisons.physical_skill: One-gripper tool transport, jaw placement, asymmetric handle squeezing through a latch point, and released retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Pliers remain self-clamped on the marked band, at least 2 cm above the table, level within 10°, untouched and still for one second; off-band or still-held states receive partial credit.
comparisons.reason: It tests closing a hand tool through a binary latch point and proving released clamping, not continuous angular-stop adjustment, concentric driver/wrench countertorque, or multi-cycle setting retention.

comparisons.objective: PR-1805 secures a bicycle wheel to a stand with a two-part U-lock; the candidate calibrates and locks a robot-gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1805 tests threading a rigid shackle through spokes and angled bent-foot crossbar engagement, not concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1805 requires correct wheel/stand enclosure and latched crossbar after release; the candidate requires a retained 90° setting, locked nuts, three repeatable cycles, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: Linking two fixed objects with an angled lock is meaningfully different from preserving an adjustable screw setting while tightening its jam nut and function-cycling it.

comparisons.objective: PR-1810 swipes a magnetic-stripe card once and returns it to a stand; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1810 tests continuous slot tracking at bounded speed and orientation, whereas the candidate tests tool seating, countertorque, and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1810 scores a valid one-direction read and released card return; the candidate scores angular tolerance, lock retention, repeated motion, and hands-off clearance.
comparisons.reason: The complete swipe rubrics establish a velocity-controlled constrained pass, not mechanical adjustment or locknut retention.

comparisons.objective: PR-1882 joins articulated chain ends with a connecting link and side-entry keeper; the candidate sets a gripper opening limit.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1882 tests multi-hole alignment and lateral keeper insertion into a loose chain assembly, not coupled screw-and-nut counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1882 requires both ends seated, keeper retained, joint cradled, chain guided, and hands released; the candidate requires a locked angle surviving three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Although both include retention, chain-link assembly does not test preserving a calibrated setting against jam-nut tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: PR-1961 fills and strikes three drywall holes flush; the candidate adjusts and locks robot-gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1961 tests loading, packing, and angle-controlled wiping with a putty knife, unlike coaxial driver seating and wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1961 measures filled-hole depth, proud material, surface damage, and knife set-down; the candidate measures retained opening angle, locking, and repeat cycles.
comparisons.reason: Material deposition and surface finishing are unrelated to coupled threaded adjustment and functional retention.

comparisons.objective: PR-2185 refits a mixer beater and guard, raises the bowl, and verifies powered start-stop operation; the candidate calibrates a gripper stop and verifies retained travel.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2185 tests slotted-hub alignment, push-turn retention, guard seating, lift operation, and controls; the candidate tests simultaneous driver/wrench countertorque on a screw and jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2185 requires retained assemblies, guarded five-second rotation, safe clearance, and stopped machinery; the candidate requires a 90° stop within tolerance after three cold cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both include hands-off functional verification, but the adjusted-and-counterheld setting central to the candidate is absent from the mixer attachment task.

comparisons.objective: PR-1916 lays two robot cables into a carrier and snaps twelve crossbars shut; the candidate adjusts gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1916 tests cable routing, ordering, seating, and repeated snap-latching without strain-relief damage; the candidate tests rigid tool use and coupled torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1916 requires both cables correctly routed through every closed link with adequate tails and release; the candidate requires a locked 90° stop surviving cycles.
